_comment: Broad on purpose, and across two aspects. The core is what makes an Age scorched at all -- burning sun,
and heat; the pool is what makes this scorched Age different from the last. `molten` in the query is
what pulls its sky and its rock toward fire without any of it being named here. Its motes are ash and
only ash: embers and flames belong to the inferno phenomenon, because they are the warning that an Age
is burning *now* and a warning that also appears elsewhere is not one. Ash is the past tense, and is
**The sky it asks for is deliberately the tamer one.** This is a hot climate biased toward deserts and
badlands, not an air that burns, so where `inferno` asks for two or three suns this asks at most for a
second; where that takes red or blue this keeps to the warm end of the wheel; and where that draws
three facets this draws one, so most scorched Ages have an ordinary sky and the odd one has a second
sun over the sand. The two words stack without doubling -- the roll takes the largest cast asked for
rather than the sum -- so `scorching inferno` is one furnace sky and not five suns.
All of it is requested rather than set: a writer who describes a sun of their own gets exactly that
one, and is charged nothing for having disagreed with a word that was only offering.
